summary: Built by CCC Company 726 from Greenville Camp F-5 (reported April 1936); a 1963 survey gives a steel tower about 100 ft tall; listed as removed.

facts.design: Steel tower with an enclosed observing room at the top (1963 survey description)
facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts page lists the tower as removed. The page gives no removal date.

events.note: Built by CCC Company 726 from Greenville Camp F-5. Reported in the Greenville Sun, April 9, 1936. The company moved into camp November 2, 1935. The completion date is not given.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: steel tower with an enclosed observing room, about 100 feet overall, owned and operated by the U.S. Forest Service.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes a 1936 Greenville Sun report and a 1963 Coast and Geodetic Survey record. The 1936 date is the report date; the record says the tower was built, not when it was finished. Two searches returned only coordinate and map directory pages and Mark Twain National Forest history pages that do not name this tower. No removal date and no current-site information. NHLR and FFLOS have no Julian entry. The record's height_m was null; 30.5 m comes from the 1963 survey's about 100 feet.
